newsitem.title: USA: L.A. County faces $357 mln projected shortfall-CAO.
newsitem.headline: L.A. County faces $357 mln projected shortfall-CAO.

text.p: Los Angeles County's chief administrative officer warned Thursday the county could face a projected countywide shortfall of $356.7 million in fiscal year 1997-1998, which will begin on July 1.

Chief Administrative Officer David Janssen said the countywide figure reflected projected shortfalls of $146.4 million in the county's general fund and $210.3 million for the Department of Health Services.

Janssen said his shortfall forecast was based on assumptions and factors that could change. His department, for example, did not project a year-end fund balance in the general fund, which could mitigate the projected shortfall.
He said the potential problems that were not reflected in these estimates included: welfare reform, California's Proposition 218 and the repayment of Medicaid waiver loans.

"The degree to which we are yet unable to support all ongoing operational costs with stable ongoing revenues underscores a significant continuing structural deficit in the county budget," Janssen told county supervisors in a letter.
Janssen said he continues to closely monitor unresolved current year budget issues, including the county's failure to secure $48.5 million in federal funding to sustain its probation operations.
"On the positive side, as previously noted, we are hopeful that fund balance will be generated and that we may witness a greater than anticipated growth in property tax revenue," he said.

The county Board of Supervisors plans to meet later Thursday to discuss these budget forecasts and other fiscal matters. The chief administrative office is scheduled to present its recommendations for the 1997-1998 budget in April.
